title: Optimization by space transformation and decomposition
contribution: A trust-region framework for smooth unconstrained optimization in which the gradient is mapped forward to an auxiliary space by R_k and the step is mapped back by T_k. It has global convergence and O(eps^-2), O(eps^-1) and O(log eps^-1) iteration bounds (Thms 3.1-3.4, pp. 24-27). Two instances follow: a parallel space-decomposition method with RAS/ASH and coarse-space correction (Thm 5.1, p. 58), and trust-region methods with inaccurate gradients, for which sharp relative-error bounds tied to eta_1 are proved (Thms 6.1-6.3, pp. 72-77).
problem_entry: Two motivations. Domain-decomposition techniques (RAS, coarse grids) are 'little explored' in optimization, and plain Additive Schwarz does not converge (p. 5). Existing trust-region results with inexact gradients are only asymptotic (p. 70). The entry move is to treat the inaccurate gradient as a transformation of the true one, R_k = g_hat g^T/||g||^2 (p. 7).
key_idea: Keep the classical trust-region ratio test and radius update, and change only the pair (R_k, T_k), with T_k != R_k^T allowed (pp. 11-13). Convergence then hinges on a consistency condition g^T T R g/||R g||^2 >= lambda > eta_1 (Assumption 3.7, p. 19). Space decomposition, inaccurate gradients and Armijo line search are all instances of this one algorithm (pp. 51, 70, 79-80).
assumptions: f bounded below with Lipschitz gradient, global 'For simplicity' (p. 14). Models share a Lipschitz constant; Cauchy-type decrease; an angle condition sin(phi_k) <= beta (Delta_k/||grad h_k(0)||)^p, automatic for Cauchy-decrease steps (Prop. 3.1, p. 19); ||T_k|| <= tau; ||R_k g_k|| >= kappa ||g_k||; consistency lambda > eta_1 (pp. 14-19). Deterministic, unconstrained, first-order, linear R_k and T_k (p. 12).
proof_devices: reduction-ratio lower bound through two angles, phi_k (step vs model gradient) and psi_k (R_k g vs T_k^T g), using the angle inequality <= phi+psi to get the factor (1 - tan phi tan psi); heuristic first-order estimate first, then rigorous version; tight for n=2 (Lemma 3.1, pp. 16-18)
radius lower bound Delta_k >= mu ||g_tilde_k|| (g_tilde_k = smallest gradient so far) by contradiction at the first violating index (Prop. 3.3, pp. 21-22)
counting successful iterations from Delta_K <= gamma1^(K-S) gamma2^S Delta_0, giving K <= c|S_K| + log term (Lemma 3.3, pp. 22-23)
'map of logic reliance': all complexity theorems use only Lemmas 3.2-3.3, which depend on the assumptions only through Prop. 3.3, so variants re-prove just those (p. 23)
lim ||g_k|| -> 0 without sufficient decrease by forbidding radius expansion when Delta_k > mu_bar ||grad h_k(0)|| (Thm 3.7, p. 33; answers Yuan's example, p. 25)
inexact oracle encoded as rank-one map R_k = g_hat g^T/||g||^2 with T_k = I (p. 70)
largest admissible region for inexact gradients, the ball ||g_hat - g/(2 eta_1)|| < ||g||/(2 eta_1) (Thm 6.3, pp. 76-77)
sharpness example f = ||x||^2/2 with g_hat outside the ball: rho_k <= eta_1 forever, Delta_k <= gamma1^k Delta_0, iterates stall within Delta_0/(1-gamma1) of x0 (Example 6.1, pp. 77-78)
problem-independent complexity enlargement factor, < 52 for one correct significant digit (pp. 73-74)
experiments: Tables 2-4 (pp. 63-69): 15 CUTEst/Powell problems at n=10^3/10^4 with m=10/100 subspaces comparing AS vs RAS vs no decomposition; coarse spaces on chrosen (n=6400) and on randomly coupled variants; a 128^2 Plateau problem with generic vs structure-aware partitions and an HEM coarse space. Iterations to ||g|| <= 1e-6||g0|| with a 1e4 cap, failures reported. Also an eta_1 x zeta sweep on 150 perturbed problems scored by a new eps-effectiveness (pp. 80-84), and an audit and patch of GNU Octave fminunc (pp. 97-98). No profiles, no timings, no code release.
positioning: Extends Lions' parallel Schwarz method to nonlinear optimization and contrasts with PVD/PGD/PVT-type decompositions (pp. 4-5). Generalizes Carter's zeta < 1 - eta_1 (p. 20). Its condition is looser than Conn-Gould-Toint's by alpha/2 while it concedes that '[30] is indeed much more general' (p. 75). Notes that probabilistic-model trust-region work (including Vicente's own) measures absolute rather than relative errors (p. 87).
writing: A long, signposted preprint: a notation table (p. 10), sections 'safely skipped in a first reading' (p. 8), a heuristic picture before each rigorous lemma (pp. 16-17), frank labels ('unsophisticated implementation', p. 62), and a playful closing line about fminunc (p. 98).
limits_future: The framework is not a specific algorithm and must be tailored (p. 61). Coarse spaces are problem-dependent (p. 61), RAS is not universal (p. 65), the generic partition fails at m=128 on Plateau (p. 69), and eta_1 = 1/2 is not covered (p. 83). Future work (pp. 85-87): LM and cubic globalization, nonlinear transformations and Banach spaces, preconditioning (ASPIN), asynchronous variants, constraints and nonsmoothness, probabilistic relative errors and random transformations, SGD.

method_links.note: O(eps^-2)/O(eps^-1)/O(log eps^-1) by function class, with the aim of preserving standard complexities. The price of gradient inexactness is a problem-independent constant, not an order change. Bounds are in iterations, and no n-dependence appears in the parts read.

PDE techniques (Additive Schwarz/RAS, coarse correction) are kept as step generators and globalized by a trust-region ratio test rather than a poll with sufficient decrease. The coarse step needs no decrease of its own, like a search step.

The accuracy requirement is relaxed to the largest tolerable region, and crossing the threshold provably and visibly breaks the method (matches step 5). The relaxation is deterministic (bounded relative error); the probabilistic version is listed as future work.
Skeleton and ratio test unchanged; the step map changes instead of the notion of success. The price is a compatibility condition on eta_1 (Assumption 3.7; eta_1 < 1/theta for RAS).
Named collection (CUTEst/Powell) with failures reported, but tables of iteration counts rather than profiles, and no code release. Practical impact comes through a patch to GNU Octave fminunc.

transferable: Encode an inexact oracle as a rank-one linear map of the exact one (R_k = g_hat g^T/||g||^2, T_k = I) so that a structural theory for transformed gradients covers it; the choice of R_k does not matter because only R_k g_k enters (p. 7, p. 72).

Bound a trust-region ratio through two angles and the inequality angle <= phi + psi, which gives the factor (1 - tan phi tan psi). Add an angle assumption on the step that Cauchy-decrease steps meet automatically with p = 1/2 (pp. 16-19).

Complexity without a forcing function: lower-bound Delta_k by mu times the smallest gradient so far (contradiction at the first violating index), then count successful iterations from Delta_K <= gamma1^(K-S) gamma2^S Delta_0 (pp. 21-25).
After the main proof, write the dependency map of which lemmas each theorem uses, so that later variants only re-prove those (p. 23).

Show a tolerance bound is sharp twice: with an exact analytic failure (f = ||x||^2/2, rho_k <= eta_1 forever) and with a parameter sweep plotting the theoretical threshold as a vertical line (pp. 77-84).

Score partial success by eps-effectiveness = min{1, log(||grad f(x_out)||/||grad f(x0)||)/log eps} averaged over the set; with an inexact gradient, stop at eps_hat = eps(1-zeta)/(1+zeta) to certify the true-gradient criterion (pp. 81-82).
To show when a component matters, inject controlled coupling 0.5 x^T V V^T x with dense- or sparse-random V into a benchmark and average over 10 draws (pp. 66-67).
Turn a threshold theorem into a parameter rule (eta_1 < (1+zeta)^-1 or eta_1 < 1 - zeta), then audit a widely used solver against it and publish the patch (pp. 84-85, 97-98).

quotes.text: We, however, take an entirely different perspective: inaccurate gradient is a transformation of the accurate one.
It is entertaining to realize that such a behavior is predicted so precisely by the theory derived from Algorithm 2.1, a framework that looks so unrelated to fminunc.

title: A Review of Multi-Objective Optimization: Theory and Algorithms
contribution: A review talk (Lehigh ISE, 21 Apr 2020, co-authored with PhD student Suyun Liu). It covers Pareto dominance, weak and strict Pareto sets, weighted-sum and epsilon-constraint scalarization with their necessary and sufficient conditions and a counterexample, and Fliege-Svaiter steepest descent and Newton's method with their convergence and complexity results (including Fliege-Vaz-Vicente 2019). It closes with a map of a priori vs a posteriori method classes and the purity/Gamma/Delta metrics (pp. 1-46).
problem_entry: A tutorial entry: define the MOP and build dominance from a six-point discrete table (no point minimizes both objectives; P = {1,2,4,5}), then the weak and strict Pareto sets with LP examples (pp. 3-10).
key_idea: Two routes, 'Scalarization methods (entire Pareto front)' and 'Gradient-based methods (single Pareto point)' (p. 2). Each gradient method is the single-objective method with a min-norm convex-combination direction and a componentwise Armijo test, recovering the single-objective direction at m = 1 (pp. 28-32). The final class map puts list-updating a posteriori methods against a priori scalarizations (pp. 41-42).
assumptions: F is C^1 with Lipschitz gradients for steepest descent, and at least one f_i bounded below for the O(1/sqrt k) rate (pp. 26, 33). Newton needs R^m-strongly convex, C^2 F with uniformly positive definite, Lipschitz Hessians and a nearby start (pp. 35, 39). No constraints or noise in the gradient part; stochastic MOO is a classification slide only (p. 43).
proof_devices: none new (review); cited results: dual min-norm problem over the simplex gives d(x) = -sum lambda_i grad f_i(x), and theta(x) = 0 iff x is Pareto stationary (pp. 29-31)
counterexample: f_i = -x_i on the unit disc, (1,0) in P_s is reached only with mu_2 = 0, so positive weights miss strict Pareto points (pp. 18-19)
componentwise sufficient-decrease lemma F(x+td) < F(x) + sigma t J_F(x) d (p. 28)
positioning: Relies on Ehrgott, Fliege-Svaiter 2000, Fliege-Drummond-Svaiter 2009, Fliege-Vaz-Vicente 2019 and Fukuda-Drummond 2014 (p. 46). Evolutionary methods are cast as having 'no theoretical convergence guarantee' and mathematical-programming methods as convergent 'for one point on the Pareto front' (p. 41). The DMS paper is not on the reference slide even though purity and Gamma/Delta are presented (pp. 44-46).
writing: Build-style slides (duplicate pages 4-5 and 11-12), a six-point table as the running example, and an unlabelled four-panel figure for list updating (p. 42). Two slips: the p. 29 subproblem is unbounded as written and is corrected on p. 30, and Algorithm 2 step 6 uses d_k instead of s_k (p. 38).
limits_future: Pedagogical only. No derivative-free multi-objective method is named, the list-updating figure is unattributed (p. 42), and no future directions are given.

method_links.note: Multi-objective descent keeps the single-objective skeleton (direction subproblem + backtracking) and generalizes the acceptance test to a componentwise Armijo condition; the m = 1 collapse is stated.

Class-native front metrics (purity, max hole Gamma, spread Delta) taught with formulas.
